value: DECLARED DURING THE VOYAGE, 2026-09-11, under ruling 2026-09-11-a-gate-reading-health-gets-a-second-shape-when-health-is-the-work. This belongs at the CAST and was not there, because the shape did not exist when this ticket was cast this morning. It is written here now rather than backdated: the subject of this repair is a RED proof. skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py was sealed red BY THE VERY DEFECT this ticket fixes (five commands named in no charter), so at BUILDME there was no honest green warrant to name and the build named an unrelated green proof, cairn/tools/cairnmap/proofs/test_cairnmap.py, to open the door. The coverage rung at PROVED caught that and was right to. Akien, 2026-09-11: 'the broken thing gets declared at ticketing to be the subject of the repair, and thus allowed this.'

2026-09-11, the full command-ownership census over the live corpus: 25 executables in bin/cmd, 75 charters, 79 invocable units (a unit is a charter plus any top-level facility block carrying its own `what`+`invoke`). 20 commands are owned, 5 are not. Of the 22 ownership SITES, 17 are the owning component's own top-level `invoke` naming the command (cairnmap, compile, determinism, edges, feedbackmap, install, operator_inbox, probescan, recordverdict, ruling, skilldial, sudorelay, test, tickets, whatsnext) and 5 are facility blocks on bin's charter (slate via session_open_program, turnscan via turn_shape_scan, askscan via prebuild_feedback_scan, deletegate and trash both via unrecoverable_delete_gate). ZERO commands are owned by a charter under bin/cmd/. Separately: `./bin/cairn cairnmap --gate` reports RED — 6 finding(s) (7 checks proved · 75 charters); the sixth is 'skill not installed: /ruled'. skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py prints 8/9, the one red being test_the_skill_class_derivation_gate_is_green. ~/.claude/skills holds 14 entries, every one a symlink into ~/dev/src/cairn/skills.

THE COMMAND LANE WALKS ONE WAY, and this ticket does not turn it around. It asks whether each executable in bin/cmd is named by some charter; it never asks whether each command a charter NAMES still exists. So a charter naming a command nobody can run is invisible. n=1 and it is inside this ticket's own scope: cairn/tools/operator_inbox's charter has named `cairn operator_inbox` while every caller in the corpus says `cairn operator`, and nothing ever reported it. The inverse check is NOT built here because extracting `cairn <word>` from prose invoke strings false-positives on bin's own literal `cairn <name> <args...>`, and a check that manufactures reds is worse than the gap. Recorded for a later cast.

The /ruled INSTALL, listed under item B6 of the build queue, rides this ticket — B5's own stated falsifier ('test_intent_skill.py goes green') cannot be met without it, because that proof's derivation-gate tooth reads the whole gate and the gate carries the uninstalled-/ruled red. B6 is not voided: its other half — SKILL.md frontmatter (name:, description:) for /design and /idea, which are invisible to frontmatter-parsing discovery today — stands untouched and is still owed.

Item B5 of the build queue, pre-approved by Akien. Cast after a census reshaped it twice: the ownership measurement killed 'give each a charter' (17 of 22 ownership sites are the owning component's own invoke; none live under bin/cmd/), and reading the proof's tooth killed 'the five names are enough' (the tooth reads the whole gate, which carries a sixth red assigned to B6).
